title: Every DNA Model Leaves Something Out

scenes.tts: The Human Genome Project took about 13 years to read human DNA. A genome is all the DNA in one set of chromosomes. By 2022, the estimated cost to read a human-sized genome was about 525 dollars. What changed? Nobody has seen DNA the way you see a pencil. We know it from evidence and models.

By 2022, the estimated cost to read a human-sized genome was about 525 dollars. What changed? Nobody has seen DNA the way you see a pencil. We know it from evidence and models.

scenes.tts: A model is a simplified picture that helps explain something real. DNA has four bases: A, T, G and C. A flat ladder model shows which bases pair up, but leaves out the twist. A string of letters shows base order, but leaves out the shape. Every model hides something.

scenes.narration: A model is a simplified picture that helps explain something real. DNA has four bases: A, T, G and C. A flat ladder model shows which bases pair up, but leaves out the twist. A string of letters shows base order, but leaves out the shape. Every model hides something.

scenes.tts: By the early 1950s, scientists had three kinds of evidence. First, base amounts. In a DNA sample, the amount of A is close to the amount of T. G is close to C. Second, X-ray patterns. X-rays shone through DNA fibers make spots on film. Their spacing pointed to a helix, a coil, about 2 nanometers wide. It gave shape clues, not a photo of the bases.

scenes.narration: By the early 1950s, scientists had three kinds of evidence. First, base amounts. In a DNA sample, the amount of A is close to the amount of T. G is close to C. Second, X-ray patterns. X-rays shone through DNA fibers make spots on film. Their spacing pointed to a helix, a coil, about 2 nm wide. It gave shape clues, not a photo of the bases.

scenes.tts: Third, model building. Watson and Crick fitted these facts together with the known chemistry of the parts. In 1953, they published the double helix: two strands coiled around each other, backbones outside, bases inside. Base pairing is the rule that A pairs with T, and G pairs with C. They called the model unproved. Later tests supported it.
scenes.visual: evidence merges into model; backbones outside, base pairs inside
scenes.narration: Third, model building. Watson and Crick fitted these facts together with the known chemistry of the parts. In 1953, they published the double helix: two strands coiled around each other, backbones outside, bases inside. Base pairing is the rule that A pairs with T, and G pairs with C. They called the model unproved. Later tests supported it.

scenes.tts: Knowing the shape did not give the order of the bases. DNA sequencing is any method that reads that order. In 1977, Frederick Sanger and colleagues published one. It stops copies of a strand at each kind of base. The lengths of the copies reveal the order. From 1990 to 2003, the Human Genome Project mostly used improved versions. It made a reference sequence: a standard to compare against.
scenes.visual: copies of different lengths sorted, reveal letters; 1990-2003 bar; reference
scenes.narration: Knowing the shape did not give the order of the bases. DNA sequencing is any method that reads that order. In 1977, Frederick Sanger and colleagues published one. It stops copies of a strand at each kind of base. The lengths of the copies reveal the order. From 1990 to 2003, the Human Genome Project mostly used improved versions. It made a reference sequence: a standard to compare against.

scenes.tts: So what changed? The double helix model still holds. Sequencing added the letters, and how they differ between people. Now that reading DNA costs far less, biologists can compare many people and species. Keep this rule: every model shows some things and hides others.
